about: Mini-stories for Story Order, written for this app at about a 2nd to 3rd grade reading level. Each story has a title and 4 sentences in the order they happen. Every story must have only one sensible order. Characters are made up.

stories.title: The Lost Kite
sentences: Mia flew her red kite at the park.
A strong wind pulled the string from her hand.
The kite got stuck in a tall tree.
Her dad used a ladder to get it down.

stories.title: Fresh Bread
sentences: Sam mixed flour, water, and yeast.
He let the dough rise for an hour.
Then he baked it in the hot oven.
The warm bread smelled so good!

stories.title: The Bean Seed
sentences: Lee planted a bean seed in a cup.
She gave it water every day.
A tiny green sprout popped up.
Soon the plant was taller than the cup.

stories.title: Snow Day
sentences: Snow fell all night long.
In the morning, the yard was white.
The kids rolled three big snowballs.
They stacked them to make a snowman.

stories.title: From Egg to Frog
sentences: A frog laid eggs in the pond.
The eggs hatched into tadpoles.
The tadpoles slowly grew legs.
They hopped out as little frogs.

stories.title: The Wiggly Tooth
sentences: Ben's front tooth felt wiggly.
He bit into a crunchy apple.
The tooth fell right out!
He put it under his pillow that night.

stories.title: Party Time
sentences: Ava made a list of friends to invite.
She mailed the party cards.
Her friends came over on Saturday.
Everyone sang and ate cake.

stories.title: Puddle Jumping
sentences: Dark clouds filled the sky.
Big drops of rain began to fall.
Max opened his yellow umbrella.
He jumped in every puddle on the way home.

stories.title: The Shark Book
sentences: Zoe found a book about sharks.
She checked it out at the front desk.
She read it every night that week.
Then she took it back to the library.

stories.title: A New Butterfly
sentences: A caterpillar ate leaf after leaf.
It grew fat and long.
It made a hard shell called a chrysalis.
Two weeks later, a butterfly came out.

stories.title: Pancake Morning
sentences: Dad cracked two eggs into a bowl.
He stirred in milk and flour.
He poured the batter into a hot pan.
We ate the pancakes with syrup.

stories.title: Game Day
sentences: The team put on their blue shirts.
The game started with a big kick.
Nora scored a goal at the very end.
The whole team cheered for her.

stories.title: Muddy Puppy
sentences: The puppy rolled in the mud.
Now he was brown and messy.
Eli gave him a bubbly bath.
The puppy shook water all over Eli!

stories.title: Blanket Fort
sentences: Jay pulled the cushions off the couch.
He leaned them against two chairs.
He laid a blanket over the top.
Then he crawled inside his new fort.

stories.title: Homemade Ice Pop
sentences: Kim poured juice into a small cup.
She put a stick in the middle.
She set the cup in the freezer.
The next day she had an ice pop.

stories.title: Duck Pond Ride
sentences: Omar put on his bike helmet.
He rode his bike to the lake.
He stopped to watch the ducks swim.
Then he rode back home for lunch.

stories.title: The Sandcastle
sentences: Rosa filled her bucket with wet sand.
She flipped it over to make a tower.
She built a wall around the tower.
A big wave washed it all away.

stories.title: Lemonade Stand
sentences: Tom squeezed six lemons.
He mixed the juice with water and sugar.
He set up a stand by the sidewalk.
He sold ten cups by noon.

stories.title: Ant Picnic
sentences: The family spread a blanket on the grass.
They set out sandwiches and grapes.
A line of ants marched toward the food.
They packed up and ate inside instead.

stories.title: Lights Out
sentences: Lightning flashed across the sky.
The lights in the house went out.
Grandma lit a candle.
We told stories until the power came back.

stories.title: Robin's Nest
sentences: A robin gathered twigs and grass.
She built a nest in the tree.
She laid three blue eggs.
Soon, baby birds were chirping for food.

stories.title: The Lost Mitten
sentences: Leo wore his green mittens to school.
At recess, one mitten fell in the snow.
His friend found it by the slide.
Leo thanked her with a big smile.

stories.title: Blue Sky Picture
sentences: Ella put on an old shirt to paint.
She dipped her brush in blue paint.
She painted a sky over a little house.
She hung her picture on the fridge.

stories.title: Lunch Time
sentences: Get out two slices of bread.
Spread cheese on one slice.
Add ham on top of the cheese.
Press the slices together and take a bite.

stories.title: Apple Pie
sentences: We drove to the apple farm.
We picked a basket of red apples.
At home, Mom peeled and sliced them.
Soon an apple pie was baking.

stories.title: Bubbles the Goldfish
sentences: Ivy bought a goldfish at the pet store.
She carried it home in a plastic bag.
She let it swim into its new tank.
She named the fish Bubbles.

stories.title: Noodle Night
sentences: Dad filled a big pot with water.
Small bubbles formed on the bottom.
Soon the water was boiling.
Dad added the noodles.

stories.title: Starry Night
sentences: The sun set behind the hills.
The sky turned pink, then dark blue.
One by one, the stars came out.
We found the Big Dipper.

stories.title: Spelling Test
sentences: The teacher gave the class ten new words.
Ana practiced them every night.
On Friday, the class took the test.
Ana spelled all ten words right!

stories.title: Where Is Rex?
sentences: The gate was left open.
Rex ran out to chase a squirrel.
The family searched the whole street.
They found Rex napping on a porch.

stories.title: On the Ice
sentences: Lily laced up her new skates.
She stepped onto the ice.
She wobbled and fell down.
She got up and tried again.

stories.title: Sled Hill
sentences: Gus pulled his sled up the hill.
He sat down and held on tight.
The sled zoomed to the bottom.
He climbed back up to go again.

stories.title: Tomato Garden
sentences: In spring, Nana planted tomato seeds.
All summer, the vines grew tall.
Green tomatoes turned bright red.
In the fall, she picked a big basket.

stories.title: Popcorn
sentences: Pour the kernels into the pot.
Put on the lid and turn up the heat.
Listen for the pop, pop, pop!
Shake on some salt and enjoy.

stories.title: A Letter for Grandpa
sentences: Nick wrote a letter to his grandpa.
He put it in an envelope with a stamp.
The mail carrier picked it up.
Three days later, Grandpa read it.

stories.title: Sick Day
sentences: Maya woke up with a sore throat.
Her mom took her temperature.
The doctor said to rest and drink water.
In two days, Maya felt better.

stories.title: The Melting Ice Cube
sentences: Ty left an ice cube on the table.
The sun shone through the window.
The ice cube started to shrink.
Soon there was only a puddle.

stories.title: Fire Trucks
sentences: Smoke rose from the old barn.
A farmer called for help.
Fire trucks raced down the road.
Firefighters sprayed water on the flames.

stories.title: Train Ride
sentences: We bought tickets at the station.
The train pulled in with a whistle.
We found two seats by the window.
We watched the fields rush past.

stories.title: The Spider's Web
sentences: A spider spun a thread from a branch.
It wove a big round web.
A fly buzzed into the sticky web.
The spider had its lunch.
